title: Displaced composers: Bartok and Stravinsky
summary: Bartok was uprooted; Stravinsky left young.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: He was very much a displaced person. For someone to feel a regional culture as deeply as he did and to be plucked out of it, it had to do something to him, and it did. It's probably what killed him.
Stravinsky did it when he was young, and that even came back to him later on. In reading an account of his return to Russia in the late sixties.
He was a more cosmopolitan person than Bartok, wasn't he? He lived in a lot of different places.
It's also easier when you're young. You can't do it when you're older. Bartok, when he came here, was--had never been away. He always went on tour, but he never lived there.
He lived in Switzerland during World War I.
I think so, because I think he was living in Switzerland and that's where he wrote 'l'Histoire du Soldat'.
Yes, that's what I was talking about.
Oh, yeah, but I don't think Bartok ever left home, except to travel.
